current.text: He is a locked-in starter at forward. Tari Eason has not passed him on the depth chart.
His minutes are stable and higher than Alperen Sengun's. Coach Ime Udoka plays his starters heavy minutes.
Steven Adams is back, so Smith plays more power forward than center.
He is not a high-usage player on this team.
Lloyd sees no reason to expect more blocks, more steals or higher usage this season.
The experts call him a safe pick with little upside. Drafting him around rank 96 is reasonable, and ESPN's rank of about 120 is a better price. Josh believes he can deliver as a late pick.
Houston has a weak fantasy playoff schedule for a March 28 end: 3, 3 and 4 games in weeks 19 to 21, so 10 games in total.
Houston has only 14 back-to-backs this season.
Houston is projected to win about 54 games. The team is expected to stay conservative in the regular season and not chase seeding.

durable.text: He is a 3-and-D role player who is around average in many categories. He will never be a star.
He is a boring fantasy pick.
He makes many threes for a forward or center.
His FG% is low for a forward or center, and he takes enough shots for it to hurt a team.
He shot only about 35% on open and wide-open threes, which is below league average. He needs to become a more reliable shooter.
His interior defense, rim deterrence and weak-side shot blocking have grown a lot. Smaller, quick guards can still beat him on the perimeter.

note: He is a stable starter on heavy minutes. He is a cheap, low-upside pick at the end of our 144-player draft. Yahoo values him at 5 USD, but he costs about 1.7 USD there and about 1.2 USD on ESPN, and he went for 1 USD in our league last season. Aim for 1 to 3 USD. His 3PM (+1.3 z vs his position) and his rebounds and blocks help a punt FG% build, since his 44.8% FG on real volume is his weak spot. Early in the season, check that he stays near 35 minutes and that his open-three shooting improves. Also remember that Houston's 3-3-4 playoff schedule makes him less useful in weeks 19 to 21.
